No new ideas today: two short problems on Lecture 5. Do each one alone,
then open "Check your result". Every question on this page has its answer:
try first, then check.

## Recall

- A wide shot shows where, a medium shot what happens, a close-up how it
  feels.
- The subject goes on a thirds line, with **lead room** in front.
- A new **beat** (a new place, action, speaker or feeling) gets a new
  panel; a movement keeps its **screen direction**.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a close-up|in the centre"}
Which shot shows where a scene happens?
:   a wide shot

    Why: The first wide shot of a scene is the establishing shot.

A character walks to the right. Where do you place it?
:   on the left third

    Why: Then the lead room is in front of it.

When does a new beat start?
:   when the place, action, speaker or feeling changes

    Why: Each change gets at least one panel.
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Panels from a scene

The next scene of *Rooftop Rescue* happens in Salma's kitchen:

> INT. SALMA'S KITCHEN – NIGHT. Water comes under the door. Salma lifts
> the cat onto the table. SALMA: Stay here, Pasha. A light shines through
> the window. NOUR (outside): Salma? Are you in there?

A panel is a quick sketch of one or two minutes: a number, a 16:9 frame,
simple shapes, arrows for movement, and a caption (shot size, action or
line, sound, time).

![The parts of a panel.](images/panel-anatomy.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Five panels · 18 min"}
1. Mark the beats of the scene, and write what changes in each one.
2. Draw one panel for each beat on a sheet with five 16:9 boxes, with a
   caption under each.

*Your product:* five panels with captions.

::: {.check}
Five beats: 1 the kitchen with water under the door (a new place): wide,
"SFX: water. 3 s". 2 Salma lifts the cat (a new action): medium, an arrow
up, 3 s. 3 "Stay here, Pasha." (a new speaker, a feeling): close-up, 2 s.
4 a light shines through the window (a new action): medium or wide on the
window, 2 s. 5 Nour's voice from outside (a new speaker): close-up of
Salma turning to the window, 3 s.

- ☐ Every panel has a number and a full caption.
- ☐ The shot sizes change with the purpose.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Panels"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a colour|a new place"}
"A light shines through the window." What changes?
:   a new action

    Why: Something new happens in the same place.

"NOUR (outside): Salma? Are you in there?" What changes?
:   a new speaker

    Why: Someone new speaks.

How long should one quick panel take?
:   one or two minutes

    Why: A panel is a plan, not the final art.
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Check and time a board

Before the team builds a scene, the board is checked: every beat has a
panel; panel 1 shows the place; the shot sizes change; feelings are
close-ups; the screen direction stays; every panel has a caption and a
time. The **time** of the scene is the sum of the panel times.

![The checklist and the time line.](images/board-check.png){width=92%}

{{< sim file="sims/board-fixer.html" poster="sims/board-fixer.png" title="Board Fixer: find the problem in each storyboard" kind="game" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Five boards · 15 min"}
1. In **Board Fixer**, find what is wrong with each of the five boards, or
   say that it is ready.
2. The ready board has the panels 3 s, 3 s, 2 s, 4 s and 3 s. How long is
   the scene? Is it under the producer's 20 seconds?

*Your product:* your score, the five problems and one time.

::: {.check}
Board 1 starts with a close-up of Nour: no establishing shot. Board 2: the
screen direction flips. Board 3: the same medium shot twice in a row.
Board 4: Salma's fear is in a wide shot, too far away. Board 5 is ready.
3 + 3 + 2 + 4 + 3 = **15 s**: under 20 seconds.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The checklist"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the board is ready|12 s"}
Five panels have 2 s, 3 s, 3 s, 4 s and 2 s. How long is the scene?
:   14 s

    Why: 2 + 3 + 3 + 4 + 2 = 14.

Salma's fearful line is in a wide shot. What do you change?
:   make it a close-up

    Why: A feeling needs a close-up.

Nour is at the right edge, and she rows to the right. What is missing?
:   lead room

    Why: She needs empty space in front of her.

One panel has no time in its caption. Is the board ready?
:   no, every panel needs a time

    Why: The team cannot plan the scene without the times.
:::
:::

## Wrap-up {.summary}

- You can draw the panels of a scene with shot sizes, arrows and captions.
- You can check a storyboard with the checklist and add up its time.
